title: Naegleria species population found in pond water of parks in Mashhad city, Can the physicochemical factors affect it?
author: Najafpoor, Zarrinfar, et al.

steps.title: Prepare ameba Page saline
steps.instruction: Dissolve the following salts in distilled water and make up to 1 L: 120 mg NaCl, 4 mg MgSO₄·7H₂O, 4 mg CaCl₂·2H₂O, 142 mg Na₂HPO₄, 146 mg KH₂PO₄. Mix thoroughly to obtain the ameba Page saline solution.

steps.title: Make 1.5% non‑nutrient agar
steps.instruction: Combine 1.5 g Bacto agar powder with 99 mL distilled water, add 1 mL of the prepared ameba Page saline, autoclave for 15 min at 121 °C, pour the molten agar into plates, allow to solidify, then store plates at 4 °C until use.

steps.title: Filter water samples
steps.instruction: Filter approximately 500 mL of each pond water sample through a 0.45 µm nitrocellulose membrane.

steps.title: Culture filtered samples on NNA
steps.instruction: Place each membrane onto a 1.5 % NNA plate that has been pre‑enriched with Escherichia coli, incubate the plates at room temperature, and beginning after at least four days examine the plates daily under a light microscope for free‑living amoebae.

steps.title: Incubate plates and identify positives
steps.instruction: Keep the inoculated plates for up to one month; plates that show no amoebae after this period are considered negative. Examine plates with a stereomicroscope for trophozoite and cyst forms; plates showing such forms are recorded as positive.

steps.title: Isolate Naegleria from positives
steps.instruction: From each positive plate cut a piece of agar containing the observed amoebae and transfer it onto fresh solidified NNA medium; incubate at 30 °C and monitor daily for Naegleria growth. Add approximately 2000 µL distilled water to the plate, then gently scratch the surface and underside of the agar with a lam edge to release organisms. Collect the resulting suspension into a 1.5 mL micro‑centrifuge tube and centrifuge for 10 min at 10 000 rpm to pellet Naegleria and remove agar debris.

substeps.instruction: Transfer agar piece to fresh NNA
Add ~2000 µL distilled water and scratch agar
Collect suspension and centrifuge 10 min at 10 000 rpm

steps.title: Extract DNA from Naegleria
steps.instruction: Use the Dyna Bio Genomic Mini Kit (Blood/Tissue DNA Extraction Mini Kit) following the manufacturer’s protocol to isolate genomic DNA from the pellet; store the extracted DNA at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare PCR master mix
steps.instruction: In a PCR tube combine 10 µL 2× Taq DNA Polymerase Master Mix (Ampliqon, Denmark), 7 µL distilled water, 1.5 µL forward primer (5 mM, sequence AAATAAAAGATTGACCATTTGAAAGTGAAAACCTTTTTTCCATTTACA), 1.5 µL reverse primer (5 mM, sequence TTTCTTTTCCTCCCCTTATTAGAACCTGCGTAGGGATCATTT), and 1.5 µL template DNA to a final volume of 20 µL. Prepare a negative‑control tube in which the template DNA is replaced by 1.5 µL distilled water.

steps.title: Run PCR thermocycling
steps.instruction: Place the tubes in a thermal cycler and run the following program: initial denaturation 95 °C for 5 min; 35 cycles of 95 °C for 30 s, 54 °C for 30 s, 72 °C for 1 min; final extension 72 °C for 5 min.

steps.title: Analyze PCR products
steps.instruction: Separate the amplified fragments on a 2 % agarose gel, stain the gel with a green‑viewer dye, visualize bands under blue light, and note that the expected product size is ~400–450 bp for Naegleria genus and ~300 bp for N. fowleri. Send the PCR products for sequencing to confirm fragment identity and genotype.
